newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain denies mistreating ETA prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Spain denies mistreating ETA prisoners.

text.p: Spain's top prison official denied on Wednesday that Basque separatist guerrillas handed over by other countries were tortured in Spanish jails.

Director General of Penitentiary Institutions Angel Yuste defended the prison system as "extraordinarily secure" and dismissed allegations that prisoners linked to the violent Basque group ETA were mistreated.

"If some decision not to hand over or facilitate the extradition to Spain of a terrorist prisoner is justified by the absence of safeguards in Spanish prisons, it's because of a profound lack of knowledge about the system," Yuste told a news conference.
Some groups in France and Portugal as well as human rights organisations have opposed extraditions of ETA suspects to Spain in the past, alleging that they would be tortured in jail.
But Yuste said an ombudsman's report, commissioned by the Spanish parliament, was "emphatic about the absence of maltreatment in prisons."
Spain came to diplomatic blows with Portugal in February and with Belgium last year over their refusals to extradite suspected ETA guerrillas.
The case of a suspected ETA gunman caught by police as he fled the scene of a killing in the northern Basque region last month revived questions about torture in prisons.
The prisoner, Fernando Elejalde, was taken to hospital unconscious and in serious condition with fractured vetebrae, a ruptured kidney and a punctured eardrum after two days in police custody.
Elejalde and officials in the Basque regional government alleged he had been tortured, but an Interior Ministry investigation cleared police of any wrongdoing in the case.
The government maintained Elejalde had been injured when he was hit by a car during the chase and further when police used force to capture him.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed about 800 people in a 29-year struggle for an independent state encompassing parts of northern Spain and southern France.
Spain has been pressing for European Union conventions that would deny political asylum to ETA guerrillas in any EU country and make it easier to obtain extraditions.
